sentence: This project updates a measure of vitamins and minerals from supplements to find which combinations help health and relates it to risk factors and mortality.
This project studies how hepatic lymphatics help the liver recover after acute injury and tests whether stem cells can rebuild the hepatic lymphatic network.
This project studies mood disorders linked to changing reproductive hormone levels in females, such as postpartum depression, to understand their causes.
This project looks for genetic causes of disorders of keratinization and studies how they lead to skin disease.
This project studies whether alcohol damage to fetal brain vessels leads to fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.
This project studies how aging of hematopoietic stem cells affects the functions of distant tissues and aging of the whole organism.
This project tries to raise levels of frataxin protein by editing the gene to correct the repeat expansion that causes Friedreich's Ataxia.
This project studies how ribosomes are made and how proteins are built in neurons, and what happens when one molecule is lost in Prader-Willi syndrome.
This project builds a computed tomography imaging method that takes less time and dose for lung cancer patients treated with radiation timed to breathing.
This project collects blood from patients before and after stem cell transplants to find which molecular factors differ in those who develop lung injury.
This project offers genomics, bioimaging and bioinformatics services that support research on nutrition, obesity and metabolic health.
This project uses biochemical and functional genomic approaches to find how an oncogenic transcription factor is linked to another molecule in lung cancer.
This project studies a molecule often amplified and mutated in human cancers and how its signaling pathways could be used to treat cancer.
This project holds workshops to find what bioinformatics resources exist locally and to plan ways to grow them for analyzing large scientific datasets.
This project studies how sex differences in interneurons of the basal ganglia shape their connections, gene expression and activity, and how these differences develop.
This project holds a conference on why cancer immunotherapy fails in many patients and on ways to activate the immune system.
This project uses imaging, genetic manipulation and computational modeling to study how different inputs and types of neurons support memory in hippocampal neurons.
This project uses imaging markers to study how Alzheimer disease patterns in the brain differ across ethno-racial groups and with socio-demographic factors.
This project tests a surgical technique that uses rib fixation to prevent abnormal forward bending of the spine after adult spinal deformity surgery.
This project studies which genetic and cellular factors control how long gene therapy lasts.
